text: been used, more extensive surgery, or cisplatin-based chemoradio- therapy.2,3,9 Treatment for metastatic disease consists of palliative radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or chemoradiother- apy.2 Cisplatin, carboplatin, paclitaxel, or topotecan may all be considered for first-line therapy; if cisplatin has pre- viously been used as a radiosensitiser a combination regi- men of cisplatin with paclitaxel, topotecan, or gemcitab- ine, or carboplatin with paclitaxel, may be favoured.3 Drugs that have been tried for second-line treatment in- clude docetaxel, epirubicin, fluorouracil, ifosfamide, iri- notecan, mitomycin, and vinorelbine.3,9 Combination chemotherapy has been investigated and many regimens have shown higher response rates and improvements in progression-free survival but not overall survival; howev- er, cisplatin plus topotecan has shown an improvement in overall survival.10 Scottish guidelines7 recommend offer- ing treatment with cisplatin plus topotecan (in cisplatin- naïve patients), or cisplatin plus paclitaxel, to all women with stage IVB or recurrent disease.
